newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Police find explosives at Moscow monument.
newsitem.headline: Police find explosives at Moscow monument.

text.p: Police removed seven packets of plastic explosives on Sunday from a huge monument in Moscow, and a radical leftist group said it planted them to protest against plans to bury Bolshevik leader Vladimir Lenin's body.

A police spokesman said the packages, containg altogether 1.4 kg (3 lbs) of plastic explosive, had been found and removed from the giant 60-metre (196 ft) statue of 18th century Tsar Peter the Great on the bank of the Moskva River.
He said no detonators had been found.

Early on Sunday, a group calling itself the Revolutionary Military Council faxed a statement to Russia's Interfax news agency saying it had planted the explosives inside the monument but decided not to set them off for fear of causing innocent victims.

It said the explosives had been planted out of "revenge against those lowly politicians who have started a foul press debate over reburial of the leader of the world proletariat, Vladimir Ilyich Lenin".
Lenin's embalmed body in its mausoleum on Red Square has been at the centre of heated public debate since President Boris Yeltsin's call for a national referendum on whether to bury it.
The president has long supported the removal and burial of the corpse, but Communists want to keep it on public display out of reverenece towards the leader of the 1917 Russian Revolution.
